title: Construction and discrete linearity of integral root transport
statement:
Let $l$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_l$ finite, and $g:X\to Y$ an isomorphism of arbitrary schemes. Use the concrete root and integral tensor sheaves [def-pur-twist-sheaves] and the canonical completed coefficient comparison $c_T$ [def-pur-integral-compact-support-coefficient-data]. Let $r:g^{-1}L_Y\to L_X$ be the prescribed inverse-limit root comparison [lem-pur-roots-of-unity-inverse-image-iso], with a proof it is invertible. There is an additive isomorphism $\phi:\mathcal O_E(1)_Y\to g_*\mathcal O_E(1)_X$ satisfying $\phi(b\otimes x)=c_B(b)\otimes r(\eta(x))$. For every section t and discrete integral scalar b it also satisfies $\phi(bt)=c_T(d_Y(b))\phi(t)$, where $d_Y$ is the constant-to-completed coefficient map. No assertion about arbitrary completed scalars is included.

theorem frobeniusIntegralDiscreteTransport
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso g]
    (r : (proEtaleSheafInverseImage g AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj
      (purTwistZlOne Y l) ⟶ purTwistZlOne X l)
    (hr : r = limit.post (proEtaleRootsOfUnityTower Y l Fact.out)
        (proEtaleSheafInverseImage g AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) ≫
      lim.map (((proEtaleRootsOfUnityInverseImageIso g).2.1 l Fact.out).choose))
    (hrIso : IsIso r) :
    ∃ φ : (SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj (purTwistIntegralModule Y l E) ⟶
      (proEtaleSheafDirectImage g AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj
        ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj (purTwistIntegralModule X l E)),
      IsIso φ ∧
      (∀ (V : Y.ProEt) (b : (purTwistIntegralConstant Y l E).obj.obj (op V))
        (x : (purTwistZlOne Y l).obj.obj (op V)),
        φ.hom.app (op V) (purTwistIntegralTensor Y l E (op V) b x) =
          purTwistIntegralTensor X l E (op ((proEtaleBaseChange g).obj V))
            ((proEtaleConstantDirectImageMap g CommRingCat.{u + 1}
              (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u + 1} (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E)))).hom.app
              (op V) b)
            (r.hom.app (op ((proEtaleBaseChange g).obj V))
              (((proEtaleSheafAdjunction g AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).unit.app
                (purTwistZlOne Y l)).hom.app (op V) x))) ∧
      (∀ (V : Y.ProEt) (b : (purTwistIntegralConstant Y l E).obj.obj (op V))
        (t : (purTwistIntegralOne Y l E).val.obj (op V)),
        φ.hom.app (op V) (b • t) =
          @SMul.smul _ _
            (purTwistIntegralAction X l E (op ((proEtaleBaseChange g).obj V))).toSMul
            ((sfCompletedCoefficientMap l E g).hom.app (op V)
              ((purTwistIntegralCompletionMap Y l E).hom.app (op V) b))
            (φ.hom.app (op V) t))

proof.text: Apply the existing tensor_direct construction to the constant Z_l-to-O_E maps, their commuting direct-image square, and the adjunct root_direct of r. Its balancing hypothesis is exactly the proved root_limit_linear sublemma. tensor_direct_pure gives the displayed formula. Forgetting the discrete O_E module structure is the required additive sheaf map; its underlying groups agree with the completed integral module by definition.
Apply the invertibility theorem to this constructed map and its proved pure-tensor formula.

The constant-to-completed inclusion commutes with the direct-image coefficient map. Transpose by the ring sheaf adjunction and test at each completed coefficient projection; both sides reduce to constant_naturality for O_E to O_E/(pi^(n+1)). The discrete module map is linear, and the normalization clause of purTwistIntegralAction identifies discrete multiplication with the completed action of d_Y(b). This proves the last formula.
